en.title: Count of Adjacent Up/Down Pattern Matches
en.description:
In the pattern, 1 means the next number is greater than the previous one, 0 means equal, and −1 means less. Count the contiguous subarrays of length pattern length plus 1 whose adjacent relations match the pattern term by term.

This site has made the standard input and output explicit; any range not given by the source is marked as this site's protocol.
en.input: The first line contains n m, followed by two lines with the array and the pattern. The source gives no value ranges; on this site 1≤m<n≤200000, array elements are in −10⁹..10⁹, and pattern values are −1/0/1.
en.explanation: Example 1: only 4, 5, 5, 1 goes up, flat, then down, so the answer is 1. Example 2: the two overlapping windows 1, 2, 3 and 2, 3, 4 match, so the answer is 2. Example 3: both adjacent windows are all equal, so the answer is 2.
hints: First convert adjacent comparisons of the array into a sequence of −1/0/1, then count occurrences of the pattern with KMP, allowing overlaps.
